Area.evidence_source: [/page/18/Text/4] For instance, those making nearlethal suicide attempts often stated that a recent bereavement, break-up of a relationship, drug addiction, social isolation or bullying contributed to their act. Programmes and interventions that already exist in UK prisons are designed to address some of these problems. For instance, visiting policies are in place to facilitate prisoners' relationships with their family and friends outside prison (HM Prison Service, 2007a). Prison visitors provide prisoners with a regular visitor from outside prison should they have no one else to visit them. Anti-bullying procedures have been introduced to reduce the overall level of bullying (HM Prison Service, 2007c). The 'Counselling, Assessment, Referral, Advice and Throughcare' (CARAT) service is an anti-drug programme available in all UK prisons designed to deal with drug addiction (HM Prison Service, 2002). Finally, the 'listener', 'insider' and 'befriender' schemes provide peer support to vulnerable prisoners, especially at times of crisis (HM Prison Service, 2007b).
